text:
Maria Lopez: Quick check — can someone run an INT4 regression for llama-2-13b on the new quant kernel? I'm seeing ~+2.1% ppl vs our int8 baseline on a small local sweep (same prompts). Posting the mini logs below.
Ajay Patel: On it. Which exact int4 config? symmetric/asymmetric? qkv per-channel? Also do you want FP8 baseline included for comparison?
Maria Lopez: Use int4 asymmetric + per-channel scaling, KV caching enabled. Please compare against our current int8 baseline and FP8 if available. Use the eval harness and also a raw throughput bench. Example bench command I used locally:
```
./tools/bench_infer.sh --model=llama-2-13b --quant=int4 --seq=2048 --batch=4 --compile=auto
```
Samir Khan: I can run this on ded-3 (2xA100). @perf-bot can you provision 2xA100 for 2h for jb-quant-1751?
perf-bot: Provisioned 2 x A100 on ded-3 for 2 hours. Job ID: jb-4482. Note: CUDA 12.1 / cuDNN 9.4, driver 535.
Olivia Chen: Small reminder — for quality comparisons use the eval harness unbatched (batch=1) to avoid mixing latency-optimized behavior with the quality metric. For throughput benching, do your batched runs separately.
Ajay Patel: Running now. Will capture ppl, BLEU-ish proxies, KV hit rate, memory, and raw token/sec. Command I'm using:
```
./runtime/bench --model=llama-2-13b --quant=int4 --compile=auto --batch=1 --seq=2048 --save-profiles=./profiles/1751023456
```
perf-bot: Job jb-4482 completed. Summary: throughput 118 tok/s (int4), p95 latency 330ms, mem 32.1GB, decode error rate 0.09%. Logs uploaded: s3://perf-results/jb-4482/
Samir Khan: Quick results from my run (ded-3): int4 (asymmetric per-channel) shows ~+1.9x throughput vs our int8 baseline, but ppl increased ~2.0% on the internal prompt set. FP8 (fp8-alpha path) gave ~+1.4x throughput and ppl delta ~+0.3% (so better quality than int4 but slower). Full CSV and plots: https://internal/bench/1751023456
Maria Lopez: Thanks. How stable/noisy are the ppl numbers? Can someone re-run the eval harness replicably (seed=42) over the full prompt set evals/repro/llama-13b/reprompt.json and post raw logits so we can A/B test deterministically?
Ajay Patel: Re-running on the harness with seed=42 and deterministic flags (disable async prefetch). Also capturing runtime profiles. Command:
```
python -m eval_harness.run --config evals/repro/llama-13b/reprompt.json --model=llama-2-13b --quant=int4 --seed=42 --deterministic
```
Samir Khan: Profiler traces attached in the job artifacts. Top hotspots: 1) quant-dequant kernel in matmul path (high GPU time), 2) KV concat / reshape ops causing extra mem copies, 3) small overhead from per-token scale calculation. I'll open a PR to fuse quant-dequant into matmul and avoid the extra copy.
Maria Lopez: If Samir's fusion PR looks good, can we do a canary (1%) rollout and rebench? Also need to ensure the A/B eval uses identical seeds and prompt order. Add rollback steps and an abort condition if ppl delta >1.0% or user-facing regressions occur.
Ajay Patel: PR link: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/615 — adds quant_fuse behind runtime.feature.quant_fuse flag, unit tests, and microbench. I've also added a smoke job for canary. I'll coordinate the canary tomorrow at 10:00 PT.
Olivia Chen: Please notify support and add the change to the release notes. Assign oncall: @oncall-eng to watch the canary window and be ready to rollback.
oncall-eng: Acknowledged. I'll be on watch for the 10:00 PT window and will follow the rollback runbook if we see any >1% ppl regression or increased error rates.
Samir Khan: I'll own the A/B evaluation and quality dashboard for the canary — will run a 24h sliding eval and post alerts if delta >1% or if any prompts degrade qualitatively. Also will include profiler traces pre/post.
Maria Lopez: Awesome — thanks everyone. Once we have the canary numbers, we'll decide int4->fp8 default recommendations for the model. For now priority: repro harness runs, fuse PR + canary, and deterministic A/B. :tada:
